title: fp-ts + Effect dual library strategy
decision: Use fp-ts (pipe, TaskEither, ReaderTaskEither) for all business logic pipelines. Use Effect/Schema only for HTTP schema definitions (@effect/schema). Do not mix in same module.
rationale: fp-ts was the original choice; Effect was introduced for schema validation. Mixing both fully in pipelines creates confusion. Clear boundary: Effect for schema, fp-ts for logic.

title: OpenAI structured output: all fields required
decision: All Effect/Schema objects used in OpenAI structured output must have every property required. Use Schema.NullOr() instead of Schema.optional().
rationale: OpenAI structured output rejects schemas with optional fields. Schema.optional() maps to optional JSON schema which causes API errors.

title: OptionFromNullishToNull returns effect/Option not fp-ts/Option
decision: Use O.getOrNull() from effect/Option, never O.toNullable() from fp-ts/Option, when unwrapping OptionFromNullishToNull values.
rationale: OptionFromNullishToNull returns effect/Option. Calling fp-ts O.toNullable() on it causes TypeORM to serialize the Option wrapper object instead of the raw value, silently corrupting data.

title: Story editor autosave via localStorage draft cache
decision: Draft recovery for react-admin forms is a localStorage cache: useFormAutosave hook + FormAutosave banner in packages/@liexp/ui/src/components/admin/common/. Debounced snapshot of react-hook-form values, key liexp:autosave:<resource>:<recordId|new>, cleared on successful submit or explicit discard, stale drafts (older than record.updatedAt) dropped on mount. includePaths option narrows the snapshot to specific fields. Wired into Story create/edit with includePaths=["body2"] so only the BlockNote article body is cached (issue #813).
rationale: Issue #813 offered localStorage or periodic API writes. localStorage adds zero server load, needs no endpoint, survives crash/accidental-nav, never persists half-valid records. Scope is the BlockNote body only — the field that is expensive to retype; @blocknote/core has no built-in persistence and react-admin v5 <AutoSave> is enterprise-only.

title: Agent skill discovery via load_skill search, not a separate find_skill tool
decision: Runtime agent skills live in services/agent/skills/<name>.md with frontmatter name, description, triggers (list), agents (list of AgentType; default all). load_skill accepts an exact name OR a task description: exact name returns the body; otherwise keyword ranking (per query token: name 3 / triggers 2 / description 1) auto-loads a clear winner or returns top-3 candidates. Skills are filtered per agent type for both the prompt catalog and load_skill. Dev-facing docs (agent-cli, agent-testing) moved to services/agent/docs/.
rationale: A separate find_skill tool duplicated the prompt catalog and added a round-trip on slow local models; folding search into load_skill keeps one tool and still recovers from fuzzy names. Per-agent filtering keeps CLI-writing skills away from the read-only researcher. Revisit (drop catalog from prompt, or embeddings) if the catalog grows past ~50 skills.

title: Persistent agent memory: mem0 (not GrayMatter)
decision: Persistent agent memory uses mem0 MCP tools (memory_search with scope, memory_add with scope, memory_forget with memory_id). Do not use GrayMatter tools (memory_search with agent_id, memory_reflect, checkpoint_save/resume). Agent IDs use format `lies-exposed-<role>` (e.g. `lies-exposed-api`, `lies-exposed-infra`). Project-wide conventions go in `__shared__`.
rationale: The AGENTS.md was reverted from GrayMatter back to mem0. mem0 is the only persistent agent memory. All memory calls must use `scope` parameter, not `agent_id`. The enforced workflow: memory_search at session start, memory_add after learning durable facts, memory_forget when facts are stale.

title: Design system source of truth: shipped MUI theme tokens over ui-ux-pro-max generator output
decision: ui-ux-pro-max v2 quick-reference lives at design-system/lies-exposed/MASTER.md, reconciled to the brand (near-black #121212, coral #FF5E5B + teal #17B9B6 swapped in admin, Signika/Lora). Shipped tokens in packages/@liexp/ui/src/theme/index.ts and services/admin/src/theme.ts win whenever the generator recommends different values (e.g. its initial slate #0F172A / breaking-red #DC2626 / Newsreader-Roboto suggestion was rejected). Only v2 style rationale, anti-patterns, and pre-delivery checklist were adopted.
rationale: Repo already had a hand-crafted hierarchy (packages/@liexp/ui/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md + service/page overrides) implemented in the MUI themes; adopting generator colors would break consistency across 384 components. Reconciling keeps one canonical source while gaining the v2 reasoning engine checklist.

title: Admin chat conversations persisted in Postgres by the agent service
decision: The agent connects to Postgres directly (DB_* only in SERVER_ENV, not in the CLI ENV) and stores conversations in the chat_conversation table (ChatConversationEntity, jsonb messages, scoped by JWT user id). The api service owns the migration. After a restart the LangGraph MemorySaver thread is rehydrated from stored history on the first message (warm-set in chat.flow.ts); no PostgresSaver.
rationale: Admin history was an in-memory Map lost on every redeploy. One jsonb row per conversation mirrors the existing ChatConversation wire shape with atomic appends. Persistence failures are logged, never fail the reply. Rollout order: deploy api (migration), helm upgrade agent env (DB_*), deploy agent.
